# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-265-266 (§§265–266)

Checked: t against the packet (identical, 58 units, 412 words, ln/p correct); every morph's bracketed Ming gloss against the packet (all match); morph lemmas against known-forms and the published glossary; every grammatical label in every note; original → `l` word by word; `l` ↔ `i`; quote marks (t, l and i counts per unit, nesting); house renderings. All edits made by script (`t` and word order untouched).

## Changes

### Major
- U38 · i, n · Quote handling wrong. The first speech has already closed at `jabuja"` (U37), so `müṅke teṅgeri či mede"` is a second, outer quotation, not an inner one; `i` used single quotes and the note called it "inside the speech". `i` also added "calling out". Done: `i` now "Having said this, and saying “Eternal Heaven, you know it,”"; note rewritten (second quotation, double quotes; mede taken as statement or imperative, Ming 知 does not decide).
- U46 · i · `i` had the soldiers as the agents and rendered talaγ̇ulba (tala- + causative, "had plundered") as "destroyed". Done: "he sent soldiers and, as he had reckoned, had them plundered until all were destroyed."; note now says talaγ̇ulba is the causative, as in U41 (reference also corrected from U42).

### Moderate
- U7 · morph, n · keleleldüdkün split as kele- + -le- + -ldü- + -dkün, against the glossary (kelele-, keleledkün, keleleldüžü). Done: lemma kelele- + -ldü- + -dkün; note rewritten.
- U32 · morph, n · iredkün split ire- + -d- + -kün (and the note cited U8, wrong), against the glossary and against U7's -dkün. Done: ire- + -dkün; note cites U7.
- U13 · i · converb ičužu turned into a separate hortative sentence and morilad-že rendered "we shall mount" against `l` "let-us-mount" and the Ming 咱. Done: "Let us draw back; and when the Qahan’s body has cooled, let us mount again then.”"
- U20 · i · bolsu is an optative (Ming 做我, morph "let us be"); `i` said "will be". Done: "‘Let us, the Tangut people, be your right hand,’ you said."
- U23 · l, i · `l` "let-us-settle" contradicted the note, the morph and U25 ("let me", Ming 折證我); `i` added an unsupported "now". Done: `l` "let-me-settle"; `i` "Thinking, ‘I have another aim; afterwards let me settle with you,’".
- U37 · i · `i` turned jabuja ("let us go", as the note says) into "let us die". Done: "If we are to die, let us go on leaning on a great word.”"
- U40 · i, n, morph · `i` "pinned him in his stockade" was more specific than `l` ("having-made-stockade") and the note admits it is a guess; lemma qorγo- "guard" disagreed with the glossary's qorγo (stockade) + -la-. Done: `i` "had a stockade made on Alashai, and took Asha Gambu,"; morph qorγo + -la- + -γ̇ul- + -žu; note says the sense may be a siege.
- U41 · n, morph · note and morph claimed keis- "stem inferred from the Ming 刮", but the Ming here is 般直到; 刮 belongs to the published keisgen. Done: both reworded to cite keisgen; reference "U32" corrected to U31.
- U43 · i, n · abudqun is second person, `i` gave "let the soldiers take … what he has seized". Done: "take the Tanguts of every kind, you soldiers, each of you according to what you have seized and what you have got"; note says čeriġüd is read as addressed; note's Ming for eimün corrected (這般, not 這般每).
- U45 · i, n · "and against the Tanguts" implied a verb of marching; Taṅγ̇udud-i is the object of talaγ̇ulba (as the note says). Done: "and, as for the Tanguts who had taken to the mountain …"; note reference U32 → U31.

## Findings refused
- U21 · doubtful reading (whose counsel; "sent to ask you"). The note already says it cannot be settled; no better reading can be had from the form and the Ming alone. Left.
- U36 · `i` omits "that matter" (teli). The word is flagged uncertain in the note and the morph; leaving it out of `i` is defensible. Left.
- U4/U22 · lemma spelling daγ̇ari- against the glossary's daγari- for the token daγ̇arižu: the glossary itself uses both spellings (daγ̇ariba, daγ̇arin). Left.
- U24 / U0 · lemma mori vs morin vs morila- for morilažu / morilaba: the glossary uses all three. Left.
- U56 · `i` leaves -že ("indeed") unrendered; the house habit is to leave closing že unrendered. Left.
- U51 · "Kitad … here the Jin state": follows the glossary's existing sense and U55–56; the Ming here gives only 契丹, but the note does not overclaim. Left.
- U24 · "brought … into line" for žüg-tür oroγ̇ulžu: already declared as the drafter's rendering in the note. Left.
- U10, U11, U12 · "have built towns", "-qun participle or hortative": renderings match l and the Ming, with uncertainty stated. Left.
